subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which statement best defines variation?
options: The differences in characteristics between individuals of the same species
The passing of characteristics from parents to offspring
A random change in the base sequence of DNA
The selection of parents with desired traits for breeding
questions.explain: Variation refers to the differences that exist between individuals belonging to the same species.

questions.q: What are the two main types of variation?
questions.explain: Variation is classified as either continuous (a range of values) or discontinuous (distinct categories).

questions.q: Which characteristic is an example of continuous variation?
questions.explain: Height varies over a continuous range of values, so it shows continuous variation.

questions.q: Which characteristic is an example of discontinuous variation?
questions.explain: Blood group falls into distinct categories (A, B, AB, O) with no intermediates, so it is discontinuous.

questions.q: Variation in a characteristic can be caused by:
options: Genetic factors, environmental factors, or a combination of both
questions.explain: Characteristics may be determined by inherited genes, by the environment, or by both acting together.

questions.q: A person has a scar on their arm caused by an accident. This variation is due to:
questions.explain: A scar is acquired during life from the environment and is not caused by genes, so it is purely environmental.

questions.q: Which characteristic is influenced by BOTH genetic and environmental factors?
questions.explain: Body mass depends on inherited genes but is also strongly affected by diet and lifestyle, so both factors contribute.

questions.q: Who is credited with the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.explain: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection.

questions.q: Which phrase is commonly used to summarise natural selection?
questions.explain: 'Survival of the fittest' describes how the individuals best suited to their environment are most likely to survive and reproduce.

questions.q: What is the ultimate source of new alleles (new variation) in a population?
questions.explain: Mutations are random changes to DNA that create new alleles, providing the variation on which natural selection acts.

questions.q: What is a mutation?
options: A random change in the base sequence of DNA
The inheritance of characteristics from parents
The deliberate breeding of organisms by humans
A difference in characteristics caused only by the environment
questions.explain: A mutation is a random change to the DNA base sequence, which can produce a new allele.

questions.q: Which statement best describes evolution?
options: The gradual change in the characteristics of a species over many generations
A change in an individual organism during its own lifetime
The deliberate breeding of organisms by humans
The differences between members of the same species
questions.explain: Evolution is the slow change in the inherited characteristics of a species across many generations.

questions.q: A population of bacteria is treated with an antibiotic. A few bacteria carry a mutation giving resistance, and over time the whole population becomes resistant. This is an example of:
questions.explain: The resistant bacteria survive the antibiotic and reproduce, passing on the resistance allele, which is natural selection.

questions.q: During the Industrial Revolution, tree bark was blackened by soot and dark peppered moths became more common than pale moths. The best explanation is that dark moths:
options: Were better camouflaged, so more likely to survive predators and reproduce
Changed their colour to match the trees during their lifetime
Produced far more mutations than pale moths
questions.explain: On soot-darkened trees the dark moths were better camouflaged, so more survived to breed and passed on the dark allele.

questions.q: Selective breeding is also known as:
questions.explain: Selective breeding is called artificial selection because humans, not the environment, choose which organisms breed.

questions.q: In selective breeding, the parent organisms are chosen by:
questions.explain: In selective breeding humans deliberately choose parents that show the desired characteristics.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly describes selective breeding?
options: Choose parents with the desired trait, breed them, then breed the best offspring together, repeating over generations
Wait for a useful mutation, then release the organism into the wild
Allow only the fittest organisms to survive naturally without human involvement
Expose organisms to radiation to force useful changes
questions.explain: Selective breeding involves repeatedly choosing and breeding the individuals showing the desired characteristic over many generations.

questions.q: A farmer wants a herd of cattle that produces more milk. Using selective breeding, the farmer should:
options: Breed together the cattle from the highest-milk-yielding lines
Choose cattle to breed at random
questions.explain: Choosing and breeding the highest-yielding cattle passes on the high-milk-yield alleles to the next generation.

questions.q: A major disadvantage of selective breeding is that it:
options: Reduces the genetic variation (gene pool) within a population
Increases the number of new mutations
questions.explain: Repeatedly breeding from similar individuals reduces the range of alleles, shrinking the gene pool.

questions.q: Repeated selective breeding of closely related organisms (inbreeding) can lead to:
options: An increased risk of inherited diseases and health problems
A larger, more varied gene pool
Organisms that can no longer reproduce sexually
questions.explain: Inbreeding increases the chance of harmful recessive alleles pairing up, raising the risk of inherited health problems.
